p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram shows the use of PCR to analyze STR sequences. (a) 2 pairs of DNA strands are shown, represented by light blue bars. The strands are laid 3’ end to 5’ end, stacked. The top pair has a dark blue region in the center, divided into 8 segments. On the left side, 2 primers are shown (orange rectangles with blue right arrows and green dots, representing dye). They are labeled “dye-labeled primers.” Text above the strands reads Locus D7S820. The top pair, under the segmented blue section, is labeled allele one; the same section under the bottom pair is labeled allele 2. The segments are labeled STR sequences. A down arrow below is labeled “PCR amplification.” Now there are 4 pairs of strands, each with a dye-labeled primer bonded to the top strand on the left end. A curved downward arrow is labeled with text reading, “run PCR fragments on a capillary gel.” The curved arrow points right to a pale gray cylinder, the gel, with 2 curved green stripes around its circumference. Below is a black line with 2 green peaks, labeled with text reading, “scan of PCR product bands derived from locus D7S820.” (b) An image of the gel, shown as a pale gray cylinder. The PCR fragments are curved lines that follow the curve of the cylinder. They are either blue, black, or green. Below is a graph with vertical axis labeled “RFU” and range 0-1800 with interval 600. Its lower horizontal axis is labeled 16-plex. Its upper horizontal axis, at the top of the graph, has units bp, range 105 to 385, and interval 70. It is not labeled. The peaks on the graph correspond to the colors of the PCR fragments on the gel. A chart has been generated below to summarize the data shown on the graph. The peaks will be listed according to color, placement on horizontal axis, and placement on vertical axis.
